about: Sourced Workiva AI use cases. The page may show only what is in this file. Every surface cites a Workiva support page; every use case cites a surface and says how sure we are that it fits. Customer names never go here.

S1.title: Where AI is used in Workiva

S3.title: Reference specific files in chat with Workiva AI

S4.title: Tips for getting useful responses from Workiva AI

availability.workiva-ai: Workiva AI, once your organization has signed the Workiva AI Terms of Use. Your admin can limit it to some workspaces or users.
availability.entitlement: Part of a named Workiva solution. Check with your Workiva team that your organization has it.

chat.name: Workiva AI chat
chat.how: The sparkles icon at the top of the screen. It follows you between files and understands documents, spreadsheets, presentations, Wdata and files.

files.name: Workiva AI chat with workspace files
files.how: In chat, click Add workspace files or type @ (up to 10 files), or right-click a file and choose Ask Workiva AI. Files must be in your workspace first. It reads text, numbers and charts, including scanned PDFs and images.

doc.name: Workiva AI in a document
doc.how: Open Workiva AI from the document, then Insert the answer at your cursor or Copy it. Use Refine to change the tone or shorten it.

advisor.name: Prompt advisor
advisor.how: Ready-made prompts by industry, from the Workiva AI chat.

sheet.name: Inline content editor in spreadsheets
sheet.how: Generates content from document sources, in spreadsheets.

sec-intel.name: SEC filing intelligence (Intelligent finance)
sec-intel.how: Analyzes filings and compares them against peers using Workiva's knowledge base.

grc-chat.name: Risk and controls intelligence (AI-Powered GRC)
grc-chat.how: A chat assistant inside GRC workflows.

control-creator.name: Control creator (AI-Powered GRC)
control-creator.how: Drafts a control from the definition of a risk.

test-steps.name: Test step and attribute generation (AI-Powered GRC)
test-steps.how: Generates test steps and attributes for a control.

flowchart.name: Flowchart visualizer (AI-Powered GRC)
flowchart.how: Builds a flowchart from process documentation, control and risk information.

risk-summary.name: Risk interview and risk activity summaries (AI-Powered GRC)
risk-summary.how: Summarizes risk interviews and risk activity.

esrs-issb.name: ESRS and ISSB intelligence (Intelligent sustainability)
esrs-issb.how: Knowledge bases that summarize ESRS and ISSB standards and disclosure requirements.

disclosure.name: ESRS/ISSB disclosure creator (Intelligent sustainability)
disclosure.how: Summarizes disclosure requirements, finds related content and drafts narrative from collected data.

fitBasis.named: Workiva names a feature or example for this job.
fitBasis.assumed: No feature is named for this exact job; it is the general chat-with-files ability applied to it. Try it on one real file before relying on it.

evidence.heard: Customers described this task in their own words (explainer evidence audit; names removed).
evidence.pattern: A pattern across several customers in the explainer audit.
evidence.workiva: Workiva itself gives this as a use or example.

useCases.task: Write the first draft of the year-over-year change narrative.
useCases.prompt: Using @[this year's file] and @[last year's file], draft the year-over-year change narrative for [section]. Explain each change of more than [threshold] in one or two sentences, using only figures in the files. Mark anything I need to confirm as [to confirm].
useCases.stays: Checking every figure, and deciding what is worth explaining.

useCases.task: Check that the narrative and the tables say the same thing before the draft goes to review.
useCases.prompt: You are reviewing @[the draft] before it goes to review. List every place where a number or statement in the narrative does not match the tables, with the section and both values. Do not fix anything; I will check each one.
useCases.stays: The tie-out itself and every correction. Keep to one section at a time for long filings.

useCases.task: Explain the GAAP-to-statutory differences for each entity.
useCases.prompt: Using @[the reconciliation file] for [entity], list each GAAP-to-statutory adjustment with a one-line plain-English explanation of why it exists. Use only what is in the file and mark anything unclear as [to confirm].
useCases.stays: The math and the adjustments themselves. Excel files need your organization's AWS model provider turned on.

useCases.task: See how our disclosures compare with peers' filings.
useCases.prompt: Compare our [disclosure topic] disclosure in @[our filing] with how [peer companies] describe it in their latest filings. List what they cover that we do not, with where each appears.
useCases.stays: Deciding what, if anything, to change.

useCases.task: Pull the key points out of a long document before a meeting.
useCases.prompt: Summarize @[the document] in [number] bullets for [who will read it]. Then list the [three] points that need a decision. Use only what is in the file.
useCases.stays: What to act on. Check each Sources link Workiva AI lists under its answer.

useCases.task: Rewrite a section to be shorter or clearer for a different audience.
useCases.prompt: Rewrite the selected section for [audience] in under [number] words. Keep every number and fact exactly as written.
useCases.stays: The final wording and every number.

useCases.task: Translate a document's content into another language.
useCases.stays: A native speaker's review before anything is published.

useCases.task: Find controls that overlap or duplicate each other.
useCases.prompt: You are an internal controls analyst. Using @[the control list], group controls whose descriptions cover the same risk or activity. For each group give the control IDs and one line on why they look alike. Do not recommend removing any.
useCases.stays: Which controls to merge or retire. Work through one process at a time for long lists.

useCases.task: Map our existing controls to a new framework and see what is missing.
useCases.prompt: Map each control in @[our control list] to the [framework] requirements in @[the framework file]. Give a one-line reason for each match, mark weak matches as [unsure], and list requirements with no matching control.
useCases.stays: Accepting each mapping and deciding how to close gaps.

useCases.task: Check each control's evidence for missing attributes.
useCases.prompt: Check @[the evidence file] against this control: [control description]. List which attributes it shows, which it does not, and anything unclear, with where you found each.
useCases.stays: Concluding whether the evidence is enough.

useCases.task: Write test steps and attributes for each control.
useCases.stays: Reviewing every step and the testing itself.

useCases.task: Draft a control for a newly identified risk.
useCases.stays: Whether the control fits your process, and who owns it.

useCases.task: Write a remediation plan for a control failure.
useCases.prompt: You are a GRC analyst. Write a detailed remediation plan for the [process] control failure described in @[the file], with steps to reduce the risk until it is fixed.
useCases.stays: Agreeing the plan with the owner and the dates.

useCases.task: Summarize risk interviews and risk activity for the risk committee.
useCases.prompt: Summarize @[the interview notes] in [number] bullets for the risk committee: the risks raised, who raised them, and anything that changed since [last period].
useCases.stays: Rating the risks and deciding what goes to the committee.

useCases.task: Draft a flowchart from the process narrative.
useCases.stays: Checking the flow matches how the process really runs.

useCases.task: Understand what a new ESRS or ISSB requirement asks us to disclose.
useCases.prompt: Using the [ESRS or ISSB] knowledge base, explain what [requirement] asks us to disclose, in plain terms, as a list of the data we would need.
useCases.stays: Deciding what is material and who owns each data point.

useCases.task: Draft a sustainability disclosure from the data we have collected.
useCases.stays: Checking every figure and the final wording before assurance.

useCases.task: Rewrite the sustainability narrative for executives or the board.
useCases.prompt: Rewrite the selected sustainability narrative for [the board] in under [number] words. Lead with what changed since [last period]. Keep every number and fact exactly as written.

leftOut.pattern: Pre-assurance anomaly review of sustainability figures
leftOut.why: No Workiva AI feature for it is named in the six support pages; XBRL outlier detection covers SEC tagging, not sustainability data.
The July 2026 press release and recent release notes were not available to check.
